decision_summary: City council approved a 60-month extension of the Flock Group Inc. services agreement on 2023-12-12 (Resolution 2023-178). The initial agreement was signed in June 2022 after a 60-day pilot; 28 fixed cameras were deployed citywide and remained in service per a November 2024 city press release.
notes: Cost figures not stated in cited sources; do not copy Kearney, Missouri figures (different state, 14 cameras / $35,000 annual). The city press release mentions a Flock transparency portal on the city website, but the portal URL was not found in retrieved sources. Cameras were slated for redeployment to state highways within the city and Buffalo County per the Dec 2023 agenda memo.

decision_summary: Sarpy County Board approved the Flock Safety agreement on 2023-07-18 (Resolution 2023-231): $46,300 initial purchase of 12 Falcon plus 2 Falcon Flex cameras, one-year term auto-renewing annually at a $43,000 recurring fee. Nebraska Public Media reported roughly 30 ALPR cameras countywide in early 2026, indicating expansion beyond the original 14.
notes: Camera count 30 reflects the 2026 reported figure; the 2023 contract covered 14 cameras. The $43,000 annual recurring renewal fee is explicitly stated in the government agenda item. Contract start uses the board approval date; service start may differ.

decision_summary: Ord City Council voted 5-0 on 2026-08-03 to remove the two Flock cameras inside city limits. The cameras were owned by Valley County, which agreed to comply with the city's resolution. Reported as Nebraska's first municipal Flock removal.
notes: The two cameras had been installed in late 2025. Valley County retained the seven cameras outside city limits (separate record ne-valley-county-so). Not marked rejected because cameras were already deployed before the removal vote.

decision_summary: County purchased nine Flock cameras at $3,000 each plus $10,000 in installation and upgrade fees. After the City of Ord's 2026-08-03 removal vote, the two cameras inside city limits were removed and seven cameras outside the city remain in service.
notes: Camera count 7 reflects the post-removal deployment; nine were purchased. Annual cost deliberately left null: $3,000/camera is a purchase price and the $10,000 was installation, not an annual figure. More than 450,000 outside-agency searches in a 30-day period were reported, per Flatwater Free Press.

decision_summary: Police Chief David Leavitt withdrew the department's FY27 budget request to purchase and deploy a Flock Safety camera/ALPR system hours before a special city council budget meeting, citing public scrutiny, the evolving legal environment, and a tight budget. Framed as a pause, with possible reevaluation in a future budget cycle.
notes: Marked rejected because the proposal was killed before any contract was signed. Decision date inferred from publication timing (Tuesday news release, ~2026-08-25); the exact release date was not printed in the retrieved copy. A Flock Safety representative had presented to the council earlier that month.
